The epistemic discipline itself — no giant task list, no diagnosis of executive dysfunction/anxiety/ADHD/depression/burnout, no invented project facts, no promised momentum/motivation/relief, no manufactured precise time estimates, a genuinely smaller (not different) if_too_hard fallback — is prompt-enforced (CONTRACT), not code-checkable. input.project: Write a 6-month marketing plan for our product launch. It needs competitive analysis, channel strategy, a budget, a content calendar, and success metrics. Due in two weeks.

output.project_read: You need to deliver a structured 6-month marketing plan covering five distinct components within two weeks, and the scope is making it hard to find an entry point.

first_move.action: Write five headings on a blank page or document: Competitive Analysis, Channel Strategy, Budget, Content Calendar, Success Metrics. Under each, write one sentence describing what you already know or assume about that area for this launch — even a rough or uncertain sentence counts.
first_move.why_this: The plan has five required components and five minutes of blank-page paralysis is usually the biggest blocker; naming what you already know about each makes the document real and shows you where the gaps actually are.
first_move.done_when: Five headings exist and each has at least one sentence beneath it, even a placeholder.
first_move.if_too_hard: Write only the five headings and leave the rest blank — a structured empty document is a real starting point.

after_that.action: Pick the one component you know the most about and write two or three bullet points expanding what you already know — specific names, numbers, or decisions if you have them.
after_that.done_when: That section has enough detail that a colleague could read it and understand the current thinking, even if incomplete.

after_that.action: List the three to five competitors or alternative products your audience might consider instead of yours, and note one thing about each — pricing tier, primary channel, or positioning angle.
after_that.done_when: You have a short list with at least one concrete note per competitor.

after_that.action: Draft the success metrics section: name two or three measurable outcomes that would tell you the launch worked, and write down how you would check each one.
after_that.done_when: Each metric has a number or observable condition attached to it, not just a category name like engagement.

output.permission_to_stop: Five headings with one sentence each is a real deliverable for a five-minute session — you have started the document.

input.project: Clean out my late father's garage. There are decades of tools, boxes, and paperwork and I don't know what to keep.

output.project_read: You need to clear out decades of your late father's belongings from his garage, with no clear sense of where to begin or what to keep.

first_move.action: Walk into the garage and pick one small area — a single shelf, one corner, or the spot nearest the door — and take a photo of it.
first_move.why_this: A photo gives you a concrete anchor point so your first real working session starts from something seen, not something remembered.
first_move.done_when: You have one photo on your phone showing a specific section of the garage.
first_move.if_too_hard: Stand in the doorway, look at the garage, and send yourself a voice memo describing what you see in that first corner — no need to go in.

after_that.action: Spend 20 minutes on that one photographed area only. Place each item into one of three physical spots: keep, donate, or unsure. Nothing needs to leave the garage yet.
after_that.done_when: Everything from that one area is in a pile or zone — even if most of it is in the unsure pile.

after_that.action: For the keep pile, decide on one place inside or outside the garage where those items will live, and move them there.
after_that.done_when: The keep items from that first area have a designated spot and are in it.

after_that.action: Arrange for the donate pile to leave — a box near the door ready for a trip to a donation center, or a message to someone who can pick it up.
after_that.done_when: The donate items are out of the garage or have a concrete removal plan with a date.

output.permission_to_stop: Taking that photo is the whole job for today.
